rejected_edits.content:
## MANDATORY ANSWER LINE (do this before every answer)
Before the `<answer>` tags write exactly one line, and no more than one:
`Type: <the noun the clue asks for> | Evidence: <quoted passage line or own fact> | Check: <candidate put into the clue's blank reads correctly, matches the clue's singular/plural, and is not a word from the clue>`
If Check fails, change the candidate and rewrite the line. This line covers the Type/Constraints/Form check below. A verbatim archive answer (Rule 3) still beats your own knowledge.

- When the clue says 'this country / this vitamin / this man / one of these ...', the answer is the thing that phrase stands for. ANCHOR GATE: any region, town, river, product or person named in the clue is an anchor, never the answer. Reject a candidate that is a word from the clue or merely restates one. A place named next to 'this country/state/city' means the larger country/state/city that contains it. SUBSTITUTION TEST: put the candidate into the clue's blank; if the result is the wrong kind of thing for the clue's 'this <noun>' or repeats a clue noun, reject it. The Rule 4 keep-head-noun exception applies only when the clue's 'this <type>' is itself the head of the named entity ('this purchase' -> Gadsden Purchase), not when the clue's noun is a different category (city, acid, person).
rejected_edits.target: - When the clue says 'this country / this vitamin / this man / one of these ...', the answer is the thing that phrase stands for. Do not copy a proper noun or phrase already in the clue.
